caveats: Harness A validates the privacy gap against its theoretical envelope (monotonicity/dispersion contracts), never against zero; dp_value entries above are single noisy draws around the true aligned intersection of 12.

Both harnesses load dsVert/dsVertClient from the v1.2.0 source snapshots via pkgload (source-tree harness contract); the installed private-lib copies are used for the registry export and the worked example client.

The released monolithic harness B wrapper could not be completed on this host: the first attempt was killed by the background-task supervisor ~57 min into gate 1 with no failures observed. The structured rerun uses the same devtools::test filters and DSVERT_* env contract but stop_on_failure=FALSE and split K coverage (full sweep at K=2 only; Count and LASSO-focal at K=2,3,5; describe/gaussian/glm_grid/survival at K=3,5). 31 of 37 Synopsis blocks were therefore exercised at K=2 only.

Two K=2 anomalies are deterministic on this host (2/2 each) and would have halted the released stop-on-failure gate: (1) 'real random-intercept LMM Synopsis' errors in the ds.vertGEE exchangeable adapter with 'signed Gaussian random-intercept correlation is invalid'; (2) 'real Poisson random-intercept GLMM grid' negative-path expect_error observes the DSI transport-security refusal instead of the expected artifact-mismatch message. Whether these are environment-specific (R 4.5.2 / package-version drift vs the release environment) or genuine v1.2.0 regressions was not adjudicated here.
Harness B runs executed under CPU contention from an unrelated dsFlower campaign on the same 8-core host; wall times are upper bounds.
